# nonvacuity: can the hypotheses hold at all?

A theorem with contradictory hypotheses is true and says nothing. A witness theorem
`∃ x…, H1 ∧ … ∧ Hk` with exactly the theorem's hypotheses, proved from standard axioms, shows they can all hold
at once. A theorem with no hypotheses passes without a witness.
